### Supporting basis
Zstandard level 3 significantly outperforms gzip level 6 in decompression speed, which is critical for this workload involving repeated reads. With 1 MB dictionary usage, Zstandard efficiently captures the repetitive JSON structure, field names, and timestamp patterns inherent in newline-delimited logs. This results in a smaller archive size than gzip, reducing disk I volume. The primary trade-off involves compression speed; while gzip level 6 compresses nearly as fast as Zstandard level 3 on single-thread workloads, it consumes more CPU cycles than higher Zstandard levels. However, since the archive is written only once, the slight increase in compression time for Zstandard is a one-time cost. Furthermore, Zstandard’s decompression throughput is typically three to four times faster than gzip, greatly benefiting the frequent random-access or sequential reads required for log analysis.

### Recommendation
Choose Zstandard level 3. The marginal increase in compression time is negligible compared to the substantial long-term benefits of faster decompression and smaller storage footprint. For 10 GB of logs with high redundancy, Zstandard’s dictionary training potential allows it to produce significantly smaller archives than gzip, even at comparable compression settings. Since you will decompress repeatedly, the higher decompression throughput of Zstandard will reduce latency during every access, improving overall system responsiveness. Gzip offers no advantage in this specific scenario, as its compression time is similar but decompression is much slower and produces larger files. Opting for Zstandard level 3 provides the optimal balance, ensuring efficient storage usage and minimal read delays for your application logs, aligning perfectly with your single-write, multiple-read usage pattern.<|im_end|>
